Updates `fast-uri` from 3.1.7 to 3.1.9
Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

Thanks to @​zekth for reporting the scheme, host, and relative-reference issues, and to @​UlisesGascon for finding the suffix-reference issue and reviewing the remediations.

What's Changed

  • ci: enable trusted publishing releases (v3.x) by @​mcollina in fastify/fast-uri#229

Full Changelog: https://github.com/fastify/fast-uri/compare/v3.1.8...v3.1.9

v3.1.8

⚠️ Security Warning

This security release fixes the following medium-severity security advisory:

  • GHSA-hrr3-gc8f-f4qj — inconsistent host case normalization via percent-encoded octets

Users of the v3.x release line should upgrade to v3.1.8.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/fastify/fast-uri/compare/v3.1.7...v3.1.8

  • a1d0da2 test: generate only relative path references
  • 9eb8759 fix: preserve relative paths in suffix and relative resolution

  • 39e6493 fix: escape a first-segment colon in suffix references
  • 745183c test: cover first-segment colon in suffix references
  • ddfc6a5 fix(SEC-03): reject non reg-name characters in domain hosts
  • d86a8d2 fix: keep a colon-first segment behind "./" in relative normalization
  • eb483b5 test: cover colon-first relative references in normalization
  • b110a35 fix(SEC-02): preserve meaning of relative references during normalization

Updates `serialize-javascript` from 7.0.5 to 7.1.4
Release notes

Sourced from serialize-javascript's releases.

v7.1.4

What's Changed

  • Fix methods containing nested functions and arrows by @​Shubham-Padkonde in yahoo/serialize-javascript#231
  • docs: add SECURITY.md by @​redonkulus in yahoo/serialize-javascript#237
  • release: v7.1.4 by @​redonkulus in yahoo/serialize-javascript#238

Note on method serialization

Concise methods ({ m() {} }), including async, generator and computed-key methods, are now serialized correctly when their bodies contain a nested arrow function or function declaration. Previously these were emitted unchanged, producing invalid output that failed to deserialize (#118). Class expressions continue to be emitted as-is.

Reporting security issues

This repo now has a security policy. Please report vulnerabilities privately through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting rather than public issues.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/yahoo/serialize-javascript/compare/v7.1.3...v7.1.4

v7.1.3

See: https://github.com/yahoo/serialize-javascript/security/advisories/GHSA-m5mm-p8h7-m29v

What's Changed

  • fix: escape </script at the end of a serialized function body by @​redonkulus in yahoo/serialize-javascript#235
  • Fix serialization of Dates with expanded ISO years by @​Shubham-Padkonde in yahoo/serialize-javascript#232
  • fix: ignore functions without mutating input objects by @​Shubham-Padkonde in yahoo/serialize-javascript#233
  • release: v7.1.3 by @​redonkulus in yahoo/serialize-javascript#236

Note on ignoreFunction

With ignoreFunction: true, function values are now omitted the same way JSON.stringify omits them, without deleting them from the input object. Functions inside arrays are emitted as null (previously this produced Array.prototype.slice.call(...) output).

New Contributors

  • @​Shubham-Padkonde made their first contribution in yahoo/serialize-javascript#232

Full Changelog: https://github.com/yahoo/serialize-javascript/compare/v7.1.2...v7.1.3
